source.title: $p$-matchings in graphs: a brief survey with some open problems

accepted.question_text: Let G=(V,E) be a finite graph and let M⊆E be a matching. Write G[M] for the subgraph induced by all endpoints of edges in M. For a graph property P, call M a P-matching when G[M] has property P. Let β_P(G)=max{|M|: M is a P-matching in G}, and let β_P^-(G)=min{|M|: M is maximal with respect to property P}. For the P-matching variants defined by this induced-subgraph framework, determine meaningful upper bounds for β_P(G) and meaningful lower bounds for β_P^-(G).

evidence.quote: Definition 3.1. Let P be a property of G, and let M a matching of G such that the induced subgraph of M, <M>, has property P, then we call M a P-matching. With regard to P-matchings, we are interested in two parameters: beta_P = max{|M| : <M> has property P} beta_P^- = min{|M| : <M> is maximal with respect to P}.
Of course the first direction would be to find good upper bounds on beta_P and good lower bounds on beta_P^- for each of the P-matchings introduced.

accepted.question_text: Let G=(V,E) be a finite graph and let M⊆E be a matching. Write G[M] for the subgraph induced by all endpoints of edges in M. For a graph property P, call M a P-matching when G[M] has property P, and call a P-matching maximum when its cardinality is as large as possible among all P-matchings of G. For each P-matching variant defined by such a property P, develop characterization theorems that determine exactly when a given P-matching M is maximum.

evidence.quote: Definition 3.1. Let P be a property of G, and let M a matching of G such that the induced subgraph of M, <M>, has property P, then we call M a P-matching.
Also for each P-matching, characterization theorems should be developed to describe when a given matching M is a maximum P-matching.

accepted.question_text: Let G=(V,E) be a finite graph and let M⊆E be a matching. For a graph property P, call M a P-matching when the subgraph G[M] induced by all endpoints of edges in M has property P, and let β_P(G)=max{|M|: M is a P-matching in G}. Is there a complementary graph parameter α_P(G), analogous to the parameters appearing in the classical Gallai identities for ordinary matchings, such that β_P(G)+α_P(G)=|V(G)| for every finite graph G?

evidence.quote: Theorem 2.4 (Gallai Identities (1959)). If G has no isolates, then i) alpha_0(G)+beta_0(G) = |V(G)| ii) alpha_1(G)+beta_1(G) = |V(G)|.
With regard to P-matchings, we are interested in two parameters: beta_P = max{|M| : <M> has property P} beta_P^- = min{|M| : <M> is maximal with respect to P}.
Recalling the Gallai identities, it would be of interest to find a parameter, say "alpha_P" such that beta_P(G)+alpha_P(G) = |V(G)|.

accepted.question_text: Let P be a graph property and, for a finite graph G, let β_P(G) denote the maximum cardinality of a matching M such that the induced subgraph G[M] on the endpoints of edges in M has property P. Let G_bar denote the complement of G on the same vertex set. Determine Nordhaus-Gaddum type bounds for β_P: what are the best possible lower and upper bounds for β_P(G)+β_P(G_bar), and what are the best possible lower and upper bounds for β_P(G)·β_P(G_bar)?

evidence.quote: Definition 3.1. Let P be a property of G, and let M a matching of G such that the induced subgraph of M, <M>, has property P, then we call M a P-matching.
It would also be desirable to have Nordhaus-Gaddum type results for these parameters, i.e., to complete the following inequalities ? <= beta_P(G)+beta_P(G_bar) <=? ? <= beta_P(G) * beta_P(G_bar) <=?

accepted.question_text: Let G=(V,E) be a finite graph, let P be a graph property, and let β_P(G) be the maximum cardinality of a matching M such that the induced subgraph G[M] on the endpoints of edges in M has property P. For P-matching parameters defined in this way, determine the computational complexity of finding β_P(G), including which choices of P or graph classes admit polynomial-time algorithms and which lead to NP-hard decision problems.

evidence.quote: With regard to P-matchings, we are interested in two parameters: beta_P = max{|M| : <M> has property P} beta_P^- = min{|M| : <M> is maximal with respect to P}.
In addition to many other results which could be of interest concerning these parameters, determining the complexity of finding beta_P is most desirable.

accepted.question_text: For a finite graph G, define a disconnected matching to be a matching M such that either |M|=1 or the induced subgraph G[M] on the endpoints of edges in M is disconnected. Let β_dc(G)=max{|M|: M is a disconnected matching in G}. What is the computational complexity of determining β_dc(G), equivalently of deciding, given G and an integer k, whether G has a disconnected matching of size at least k?

evidence.quote: Example 3.5 (Disconnected matching). A matching M is disconnected if |M| = 1 or <M> is disconnected. We have beta_dc(G) = max{|M| : M is disconnected matching} and beta_dc^-(G) = min{|M| : M is maximal disconnected matching}.
Of the matching varieties discussed in Section 3, this leaves only the complexity of beta_dc in question.
